exposure: management strategy (immediate termination vs. conservative management)
outcome: perinatal complications (RDS at birth, APGAR scores, resuscitation, HIE)
cohort: The study included 150 term antenatal women presenting with decreased fetal movements to a tertiary care hospital in Thrissur, India, from January to December 2020.
finding: Maternal perception of decreased fetal movements is a predictor of adverse obstetric and neonatal outcomes, with immediate termination of pregnancy leading to significantly more perinatal complications, caesarean sections, and instrumental deliveries compared to conservative management.
mod_finding: Caesarean sections and instrumental deliveries were significantly more common in the immediate termination of pregnancy group compared to the conservatively managed group.
